title: What an ATS scanner should check before you apply
excerpt: Learn the resume structure, keyword, and formatting checks that help reduce avoidable screening issues.
author: CareerBOT Team
body: An ATS scan is not magic — it's mostly pattern matching against the job description. Before you apply, run through the same checks the system does.
First, keyword coverage: does your resume include the exact skill and tool names from the posting, not just close synonyms? "Node.js" and "NodeJS" can be read differently depending on the parser.
Second, section headers: use conventional labels like "Experience" and "Education" rather than creative alternatives. Non-standard headers are a common reason content gets dropped during parsing.
Third, formatting: single-column layouts, standard fonts, and no embedded text inside images. Anything the parser can't read is treated as if it doesn't exist.
Finally, file format: export as PDF unless the posting specifically asks for DOCX. Most modern ATS platforms handle PDF text extraction reliably, and it preserves your formatting exactly as designed.
